final_message:
The oracle provider now emits a `FixedIn` entry per (version, architecture), with an `Arch` key, when the fix differs by arch. Otherwise it emits one arch-less entry per version. The full suite gives 911 passed and 15 failed. All 15 failures are in `tests/quality/test_configure.py`, and the ones I looked at fail on a missing `yardstick` module. I didn't investigate beyond that.

- **Running the tests:** `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` as written in `CLAUDE.md` fails at import because `vunnel` isn't installed in the venv. I ran everything with `PYTHONPATH=src` in front.
- **Parsing:** In the OVAL data, an "Oracle Linux arch is X" criterion applies to the packages in its enclosing criteria block. The parser (`oval_parser.py`) previously flattened all of these, so arch was lost. It now tracks the arch for each package version it finds.
- **Collapsing rule:** I applied the rule per package (name plus module).
  - If every version of a package covers all the arches seen for that package, it emits arch-less entries, one per version.
  - Otherwise it emits one entry per (version, arch). This includes the mixed case where one version covers every arch and another covers only some.
  - A package that appears on only one arch ends up arch-less.
- **Schema:** I added `schema/vulnerability/os/schema-1.1.1.json`, which is 1.1.0 plus an optional string `FixedIn.Arch`. Only `providers/oracle/__init__.py` advertises 1.1.1, and the other providers are unchanged. The two oracle snapshots changed only in their schema URL.
- **Test:** `test_parse_arch` uses a new fixture, `mock_arch_data`. It covers the rsyslog case from the request (`8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3` on aarch64, `8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3` on x86_64), a fix shared by both arches, and two rebuilds that each ship on both.

I also wrote `answer.json` in the repo root with the one-sentence summary.

cd /tmp/bsvc-yhi_zcfw/vunnel; python3 - <<'EOF'
def pkgs(arch, items):
    return f'<criteria operator="AND"><criterion test_ref="t" comment="Oracle Linux arch is {arch}"/><criteria operator="OR">' + "".join(
        f'<criteria operator="AND"><criterion test_ref="t" comment="{n} is earlier than {v}"/><criterion test_ref="t" comment="{n} is signed with the Oracle Linux 7 key"/></criteria>' for n,v in items) + '</criteria></criteria>'
def d(i, groups):
    return f'''<definition id="oval:com.oracle.elsa:def:{i}" version="1" class="patch"><metadata><title>ELSA-{i}: x security update (IMPORTANT)</title><affected family="unix"><platform>Oracle Linux 7</platform></affected><reference source="elsa" ref_id="ELSA-{i}" ref_url="https://linux.oracle.com/errata/ELSA-{i}.html"/><description>d</description><advisory><severity>IMPORTANT</severity><issued date="2022-01-01"/><cve href="https://linux.oracle.com/cve/CVE-{i}.html">CVE-{i}</cve></advisory></metadata><criteria operator="AND"><criterion test_ref="t" comment="Oracle Linux 7 is installed"/><criteria operator="OR">{"".join(groups)}</criteria></criteria></definition>
'''
body = d("2022-4803", [pkgs("aarch64",[("rsyslog","8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3")]), pkgs("x86_64",[("rsyslog","8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3")])])
body += d("2022-0001", [pkgs("aarch64",[("foo","1.0-1.el7")]), pkgs("x86_64",[("foo","1.0-1.el7")])])
body += d("2022-0002", [pkgs("aarch64",[("bar","1.0-1.el7"),("bar","1.0-2.el7")]), pkgs("x86_64",[("bar","1.0-1.el7"),("bar","1.0-2.el7")])])
x='<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n<oval_definitions xmlns="http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-definitions-5" xmlns:oval="http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-common-5"><generator><oval:product_name>Oracle Errata System</oval:product_name></generator><definitions>\n'+body+'</definitions></oval_definitions>\n'
open('tests/unit/providers/oracle/test-fixtures/mock_arch_data','w').write(x)
EOF
cat >> tests/unit/providers/oracle/test_oracle.py <<'EOF'


def _fixed_in(vuln_dict, vuln_id):
    _, record = vuln_dict[(vuln_id, "ol:7")]
    return sorted(
        ((f["Name"], f["Version"], f.get("Arch")) for f in record["Vulnerability"]["FixedIn"]),
        key=lambda t: (t[0], t[1], t[2] or ""),
    )


def test_parse_arch(tmpdir, helpers):
    subject = parser.Parser(workspace=workspace.Workspace(tmpdir, "test", create=True))
    vuln_dict = subject._parse_oval_data(helpers.local_dir("test-fixtures/mock_arch_data"), subject.config)

    # the fix differs by architecture: one entry per (version, arch)
    assert _fixed_in(vuln_dict, "ELSA-2022-4803") == [
        ("rsyslog", "8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3", "x86_64"),
        ("rsyslog", "8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3", "aarch64"),
    ]
    # a single fix shared by every architecture: arch-less
    assert _fixed_in(vuln_dict, "ELSA-2022-0001") == [("foo", "1.0-1.el7", None)]
    # several rebuilds, each shipped for all architectures: one arch-less entry per version
    assert _fixed_in(vuln_dict, "ELSA-2022-0002") == [("bar", "1.0-1.el7", None), ("bar", "1.0-2.el7", None)]
EOF
sed -i 's/result.version == "1.1.0"/result.version == "1.1.0"/' tests/unit/test_provider.py
PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8

cd /tmp/bsvc-yhi_zcfw/vunnel; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | grep FAILED | grep -v yardstick; echo '{"summary": "The oracle provider now emits per-architecture FixedIn entries (with an Arch key) when the fix differs by arch and arch-less entries otherwise, and advertises the new OS schema 1.1.1 with an optional FixedIn.Arch."}' > answer.json; git status --short
